## PM · review of PR #5579 — you measured the equivalence instead of assuming it

I wrote "⚠️ Do not assume the inline copy and the module agree… a 'pure refactor' that quietly changes a sharing-width comparison in a security-adjacent file is the worst outcome available here." You answered it with a number rather than a reassurance:

> verified equivalent before the swap, over the full domain of both dials plus `undefined`, the rejected legacy aliases and prototype-chain keys: **144 input pairs, zero disagreements**.

Prototype-chain keys is the detail that shows the domain was actually thought about rather than enumerated — `'constructor' in OWD_WIDTH` is exactly the kind of thing an `in` check gets wrong and a `Record` lookup hides. You also identified the module's extra `!!` guards as redundant *at this call site* and said why (both dials already normalised to `''`, and `'' in OWD_WIDTH` is false regardless), rather than deleting them or silently inheriting them.

### The agreement pin is the substantive half, and it refuses the tautology by name

Triage ruled the pin, not the import swap, was the deliverable. You built the version that can actually fail, and stated the rejected alternative:

> asserting that the panel CALLS `isExternalWider` would prove nothing about whether the comparison is the same one — a re-inlined copy calls nothing at all, and a call spy stays green when the `(internal, external)` arguments are swapped.

So the assertion runs **across the boundary the drift would cross**: both surfaces, the full 5×5 dial cross-product, each verdict read off **what it renders** rather than off an internal symbol, with all three legs required to agree.

Three separate anti-vacuity guards, each closing a different way the sweep could pass while proving nothing:

- **Which pairs are violations, pinned by name** (`private → public_read`, `private → public_read_write`, `public_read → public_read_write`) — because three-way agreement alone survives every leg going silently false.
- **The half-rendered branch guard** — amber styling *and* the "wider" copy both read, throwing if they disagree, so a half-updated branch cannot read as "calm".
- **Row-existence assertion** on every pair, because otherwise "not flagged" is indistinguishable from "never rendered".

Including `controlled_by_parent` on **both** axes deliberately — "off the axis never trips D11 is exactly the kind of edge a re-inlined copy gets wrong" — is the fixture choice I would have missed.

### The question I asked, answered

`PackageOwdOverviewPanel` was **already** calling the shared module; the Settings tab was the one surface that was not. So there was no second inline copy to widen scope over, and you used the overview as the second leg of the pin rather than touching it. That is the right use of a read-only neighbour.

Documenting the argument-order trap in the code comment — "the module takes `(internal, external)`, the reverse of how the violation reads" — is worth its two lines; that is the drift the call spy would have missed.

### Scope

Path surface (`get_files`): 3 files, all `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/**` plus the changeset. Held to "exactly this convergence" as triage required; `owd-sharing.ts` untouched, as fenced.

⚠️ **A correction I owe on my own claim, not on your work:** I declared round 3's batch "pairwise disjoint by construction". It is not — **#5521** turned out to live in `packages/app-shell/src/console/home/`, the same package as this card, because I fenced that one to the wrong package. Your surface and its surface share no file and no directory, so the practical risk is nil and the merge queue serialises the landings anyway — but the guarantee I asserted was wrong, and it is recorded on #5521 and here rather than quietly dropped.

CI has not converged. No verdict and no enqueue until the gate jobs read `completed: success` by name.

## PM · addendum — the two-ablation design justifies both halves of the pin

Your report landed after my review, and it contains the best reasoning in it. Recording it separately because it is the part a future reader should copy.

You ran **two** ablations with *different predicted directions*, and the second is the one that matters:

- **A — re-inline a drifted (`>=`) copy into `ObjectSettingsPanel`.** Predicted the agreement leg red; observed red, naming all three pairs as `ObjectSettingsPanel=true PackageOwdOverviewPanel=false isExternalWider=false`.
- **B — refine D11 in the shared module only (`>` → `>=`).** Predicted the agreement leg stays **GREEN** — because after convergence all three legs delegate to one implementation, so they move together — and the **non-vacuity anchor** fires instead. Observed exactly that: anchor red on three extra pairs.

> The two halves of the pin catch different failure modes, which is why both are present.

That is the insight. **Convergence makes the agreement test blind to a change in the rule it converged on.** An agreement-only pin would have been perfectly green while D11 silently changed meaning for every author — the very class of failure this card exists to close, reintroduced by the fix for it. The named-violations anchor is therefore not belt-and-braces; it is the only leg that can see that mutation. Most pins in this repo would have shipped with leg one alone and looked rigorous.

Two more things confirmed rather than assumed:

- **The copies genuinely agreed** — 144 input pairs, zero disagreements, over both dials plus `undefined`, the rejected legacy aliases (`read` / `read_write` / `full`) and the prototype-chain keys `in` actually reaches (`toString`, `constructor`, `__proto__`). So "behaviour-preserving" is a measurement here, not a hope, and the security-adjacent risk I flagged did not materialise.
- **`PackageOwdOverviewPanel` is not a second inline copy** — it already imports `isExternalWider` at line 34 and calls it at line 204. The Settings tab was the only surface not calling the shared module, so no extra finding was needed and none was invented.

The declared lint narrowing is argued to the point of being checkable: `tseslint.configs.recommended` with no `project` / `projectService` means linting is per-file syntax-only, so each verdict is a pure function of that file's own bytes plus the shared config — and the changeset `.md` is not selected by the `**/*.{ts,tsx}` glob. That is why the narrowing excludes nothing, stated as an argument rather than an assurance.

Noting the pre-build TS2307 run as a stale-closure trap **and deleting its log before the real run** is the same broken-gauge discipline two other cards hit this session. A stale red log left lying around is how a false finding gets quoted later.

Review conclusion unchanged; CI still converging.
